Dashboard items of a dialog reading a CSV table

Source: R/dialogs.R
build.container.get.table.Rd

Builds the items of a dashboard dialog which reads a CSV file chosen by the user and maps its columns to the columns a dashboard needs, with the classes it needs: a file input, one select input per needed column (filled with the column names of the file), and Load and Cancel buttons, with the services reading, checking and converting the table.

Usage

build.container.get.table(
  name,
  classes,
  outputvar = name %>% paste("out", sep = "."),
  fileSelectTitle = "Select input CSV file",
  loadButtonTitle = "Load selected file",
  containerType = "fluidPage",
  ...
)

Arguments

name

Name of the dialog container item; the other items are named after it.

classes

Named list: the names of the columns the dashboard needs and, for each, the accepted classes (columns of other classes are converted to the first one).

outputvar

Name of the variable receiving the table (kept for backward compatibility).

fileSelectTitle, loadButtonTitle

Labels of the file input and of the load button.

containerType

Type of the dialog container item, like "fluidPage" or "wellPanel".

...

Other fields of the container item.

Value

A named list of dashboard items, to add to the items of a dashboard configuration.

Details

Messages are kept in session$userData$temp: <name>.failmsg about reading the file ("Ok", "Please choose a CSV file.", "Selected table has no column names" or "File read failed for some reason!") and <name>.failmsg2 about the column classes ("Ok" or "Column x cannot be coerced to y!").

See also

rvisDashboard, and the dashboards guide.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
classes <- list(caseID = c("character", "factor"), timestamp = "POSIXct")
items <- build.container.get.table("my_dialog", classes = classes, containerType = "wellPanel")
runDashboard(list(layout = "my_dialog", items = items))
} # }
